newsitem.title: INDIA: Gandhi suffered partition in pain, aide says.
newsitem.headline: Gandhi suffered partition in pain, aide says.

text.p: Mahatma Gandhi suffered in pain as India won freedom from colonial rule on this day 50 years ago.

"Gandhi observed the day by fasting, praying and spinning. But he was in deep anguish because of the communal riots that had broken out in different parts of Calcutta," recalls 86-year-old Jugal Chandra Ghosh, one of the independence leader's aides.
Ghosh said that Gandhi was very upset by the religious riots that broke out after the partition of the subcontinent into secular but Hindu majority India and Moslem Pakistan.
"I did not want this freedom," Ghosh recalls Gandhi as often murmuring.
Ghosh was 36 when Gandhi, reverently called Gandhiji, arrived in Calcutta on August 12, 1947.
"Gandhiji arrived in Beliaghatha to voice his protests against the communal riots and restore peace. He arrived here amid noisy demonstration by Hindu youths," Ghosh said.
"Even stones were hurled at the house, but Gandhi maintained his calm and met representatives of the angry youths," he said.
Ghosh said Gandhi became agitated on September 1, 1947, when simmering violence flared up again, leading to two deaths near the house where he was staying.
"Gandhiji was visibly upset. He almost cried in pain and took a strong decision to go on a fast unto death to counter violence."
"The leaders could not remain silent. They pleaded with Gandhi to break his fast, but Gandhi remained unmoved." Ghosh said.

"I could not tolerate his pain. I was deeply moved by his anguish. I went out and mobilised a number of youths who actively took part in the riots and got them to surrender before Gandhiji," Ghosh recalled.
Ghosh said he fought for 38 years to persuade the government to take over the house where Gandhiji stayed for 26 days.
A marble plaque above the house, once owned by the Nabob of Dhaka, now in Bangladesh, recorded its significance.
"Gandhi came to this house on August 12, 1947 to restore peace in communal riot torn Calcutta... He left Calcutta for Delhi on September 7," it said.
